text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high egress connection errors from az1a affecting inference tier (detected by dataplane monitors). spike in EConnReset and 502s. paging oncall_sre

oncall_sre: acked — joining. seeing token latency spike in metrics dashboard. which hosts?

eng-network: saw ENI queue drop on a subset of g5 nodes in az1a. kernel rx drop counters rising. also NLB target unhealthy flapping reported.

oncall_sre: noted customer error rate increase for /v1/generate and chat endpoints ~2.4% -> 9% in last 5m. spike coincides with AZ egress errors. tagging high-priority.

infra-oncall: running quick health checks: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=az1a` and `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep az1a`

eng-network: stack traces show kernel nic reset on cirrus kernel version on some hosts. Suspect host-level NIC OOM / TX sched delay. We should avoid node reboot until we steer traffic.

product-sre: customer-impact note: several enterprise customers on Dedicated pools in az1a reporting increased latency and 5xxs. CS notified major accounts.

customer-success: sending heads-up to affected customers now. included temporary mitigation note: we are steering traffic and will follow up.

oncall_sre: plan: 1) divert new inference traffic away from az1a -> az1b/usw2a fallback pool via routing policy, 2) disable autoscaler in az1a to avoid thrashing, 3) coordinate controlled node reboots for suspected hosts. Any objections?

eng-network: +1 to routing shift. create rollback policy if capacity in fallback gets saturated. watch KV cache warmup impact.

ops-bot: ACTION: updated routing policy `route-policy:az-priority` weights: az1a=0, az1b=60, usw2a=40. Propagation ~30s.

oncall_sre: verifying traffic shift. dashboard shows drop in 5xx from 9% -> 3% after routing change. token latency improved but some customers still see errors due to sticky sessions and K/V cache misses.

eng-network: investigating NLB target groups — some targets in az1a show `unhealthy` with reason `connection-reset`. posting healthcheck logs:

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway - backend conn reset
liveness probe: /health returned 200 but tcp reset observed during request
netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l => high
```

infra-oncall: initiating controlled drain of 3 suspect nodes (ids i-0abc..., i-0def..., i-0ghi...). Will `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then hold. No reboot until confirm flows are drained.

oncall_sre: please annotate incident in statusboard and set severity=sev2 for now. Also start incident timeline.

eng-network: quick test: `ethtool -S eth0` shows tx drops and queue length increases. Suggest kernel driver backport may have regressed — filing kernel bug, but mitigation is traffic steering and node recycle.

customer-success: update: one large customer (acct-3492) reports intermittent 502s during the shift window. They want ETA. Suggest message: "We are routing your requests to healthy capacity in other AZs; short degradation expected while we rebalance caches. Will follow up when stable."

oncall_sre: sent message to acct-3492.

ops-bot: NOTE: autoscaling paused for inference-pool-az1a; can resume after healthy state confirmed.

infra-oncall: drain started. pods are terminating, & traffic counts to drained instances dropping. Initiating node reboot sequence one at a time after drain completes.

eng-network: cross-AZ egress qps is rising; watch cost and warmup. Suggest pre-warming K/V caches by priming top prompt sets for heavy customers to reduce error surface.

product-sre: agree. kick off a small synthetic workload against fallback pools to warm caches and validate SLOs.

oncall_sre: monitor for cascading backpressure in az1b/usw2a. If overload detected, we will enable canary fallback to compatible quantized variants (lower memory) to preserve throughput.

eng-network: after first node reboot, NIC counters reset and system logs show no immediate kernel panic. Target health for that node returned healthy in NLB.

oncall_sre: yay — 5xxs trending down to ~0.8%. Keeping routing weight at 0 for az1a while we finish reboots and ensure sustained health.

customer-success: customers acknowledging improved performance. leaving a note to Ops to prepare post-incident comms and timelines.

ops-bot: INCIDENT: mitigation in progress. current state: traffic rerouted, 3 nodes drained and rebooted (1/3 complete), autoscale disabled, customers notified.

eng-network: timeline note: likely root cause - kernel network driver regression under high ENI queue depth leading to tx/rx queue starvation. Will follow up with AMI/kernel roll plan for affected fleets.

product-sre: next steps: schedule postmortem, determine if we need an emergency AMI rollback or kernel patch, and evaluate improved health-checks to detect early NIC resource starvation.

oncall_sre: assigning follow-ups: eng-network -> kernel RCA and patch plan; infra-oncall -> automated canary for node draining and reboot; product-sre -> customer comms draft; customer-success -> customer follow-ups.

customer-success: will send wrap-up to affected accounts with timeline and root-cause hypothesis once RCA draft is ready.

oncall_sre: closing the immediate page. leaving thread open for handoff to next shift. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation): traffic restored and node health OK. Postmortem scheduled.
